# Master Playbook — cache-resident core
The Tier-1 assistant loads this every request. Authority: the **Lessons** (`lessons.md`) outrank everything here; this guide and the strategy specs outrank the distilled library; the library outranks any ingested book. Verdicts are **TAKE / SKIP / ADJUST** (ADJUST = exactly one level moved). R:R floors (2.0 SMC/Fib, 1.3 blended EMA) and 1% sizing are enforced by the detector — never re-derive them.

## Start Here — regime + news + correlation
## Before any trade — 3 checks, in order

**Step 1. What kind of market is the daily chart? (pick one)**
Zoom out to the D1 chart, look at the last ~2 months, and match it to one of these four pictures. This one decision filters more bad trades than everything else combined.

#### Trend
Price climbs (or falls) in stairsteps. Pullbacks are small. It keeps making new highs (or lows).
SMC: with-trend onlyFIB: bestEMA: NO

#### Range
Price bounces between a ceiling and a floor, touching each several times. Flat overall.
SMC: best (at the edges)FIB: weakEMA: best

#### Wild / news-driven
Huge bars in both directions, gaps, no rhythm. Recent shock still echoing.
SMC: suspiciousFIB: NOEMA: only extreme

#### Turning point
A long trend just broke its pattern for the first time. Old direction dead, new one unproven.
SMC: often goodFIB: too earlyEMA: case by case
Remember your answer — every strategy tab starts by using it.

**Step 2. Is big news close?**
Look at the event lines the chart draws ahead of the current bar.
[NO] High-impact event within ~12h (rate decision, CPI, jobs report) → SKIP or wait for it to pass [NO] The setup itself was created by a news candle → SKIP [YES] Only minor events, or nothing → continue
Trading indices, gold, or oil? US-dollar events count as "your" news regardless of the symbol.

**Step 3. Am I already in this bet?**
Trades on related symbols are **one bet, not two**. If you already hold a same-direction trade in the same family (another EUR pair, another yen pair, another risk-on bet like an index + AUD), the new alert must be clearly better than the one you're in — usually it isn't.
[YES] No related position → continue[WARN] Related position open → new trade needs to be clearly better, else SKIP
Full family table in **Rules & Edits**. Hard caps: 3% total open risk, 2% per idea.
**Automatic skips, no discussion:** big news inside the trade's lifetime · entering late Friday (weekend gap risk) · chart is post-news chaos · you can't say why you're taking it in one sentence · you just lost twice and want it back.
**Already handled by the system — don't re-check:** position size is exactly 1%, stop is beyond the invalidation point, reward-to-risk already cleared the floor, the signal bar is closed. Spend your minute on _context_, not math.
**Now open the tab for the strategy that fired** and answer its questions top to bottom.

## SMC — Liquidity Sweep + Structure Shift (checklist)
## SMC — Liquidity Sweep + Structure Shift
Reward **2.5–4× risk**Wins **~40–45%** of the time**Loses more often than it wins** — big winners pay for it
**The idea in one sentence:** price spiked through an obvious low (or high) where people's stop-losses sit, grabbed them, snapped back, and then broke the small structure the other way — proof the reversal is real. The whole picture:

**What the computer already checked (don't redo it)**
- The swept level was a real one (a swing low/high, matched lows/highs, or yesterday's/last week's extreme — labelled on the chart)
- The spike wasn't too shallow or too deep, and price closed back inside within one bar
- The shift was a real body-close beyond the last swing, within 6 bars
- Reward is at least 2× risk; size is exactly 1%

### Walk these in order — any NO means SKIP

**Step 1. Does the regime allow it?**
From **Start Here**: in a **range**, sweeps of the range's edges are the best version of this trade. In a **trend**, only take sweeps that point _with_ the trend (a dip swept in an uptrend). Fading a strong trend is how this strategy kills accounts.
[YES] Range edge, or with-trend → continue[NO] Against a strong daily trend → SKIP

**Step 2. Was the swept level worth sweeping?**
The chart labels the pool type. Best: **matched lows/highs** (two+ bottoms at the same price — a pile of stops). Good: recent clean swing, yesterday's/last week's extreme, or the "D1 confluence" flag (the daily chart cares about this level too). Weak: lows formed months apart, or during dead overnight hours.
[YES] Obvious, recent, clean level → continue[NO] Stale or flimsy level → SKIP

**Step 3. Was the sweep one convincing stab?**
[YES] Fast stab & snap back → continue[NO] Grind, deep push, or weak reclaim → SKIP[NO] The sweep bar was a news candle → SKIP

**Step 4. Did the shift have force?**
No force = the "reversal" has no buyer behind it, and the entry zone below is guesswork.
[YES] Powerful breaking candle → continue[NO] Weak drift over the line → SKIP

**Step 5. Is the entry zone fresh?**
The shaded zone works because orders were left behind there. The **first** return to it is the trade. If price already dipped back through it once, those orders are spent.
[YES] Untouched since the shift → continue[NO] Already revisited → SKIP

**Step 6. Does the target have a clear road?**
The target should be the next obvious level _above_ (for longs) that price hasn't touched yet. If another big level or round number sits between entry and target, the move may die there — either skip, or pull the target in front of the obstacle (one edit only, see Rules & Edits).
[YES] Clear road to an untouched level → continue[WARN] Obstacle mid-way → pull TP in front of it, or SKIP

**Step 7. Timing sanity**
[YES] Sweep happened in London/NY hours → best [WARN] Overnight-hours sweep → weaker, needs everything else A-grade [NO] Late Friday → SKIP
**All seven passed → TAKE.** One "meh" answer on steps 3 or 4 → SKIP; those two questions decide most SMC trades. This strategy is _supposed_ to lose often — only A-grade setups keep the math working.

## Deep Fib — Buy the Trend at a Discount (checklist)
## Deep Fib — Buy the Trend at a Discount
Reward **2.5–5× risk**Wins **~45–50%**Banks half at the old high, **runs the rest**
**The idea in one sentence:** a real trend made a strong push (the "leg"), price has now pulled back deep into that leg — the 61.8–78.6% "discount zone" — and printed a reversal candle there, so you join the trend cheaply with a tight stop. The whole picture:

**What the computer already checked (don't redo it)**
- Trend confirmed two ways (rising swing pattern + price above a rising average)
- The leg is big enough to matter and is the one currently being retraced
- The trigger candle is a genuine engulfing or hammer that actually reached the zone
- Stop past the 88.6% line; reward at least 2× risk to the first target

### Walk these in order — any NO means SKIP

**Step 1. Is the trend young enough?**
Count the pushes the trend has already made. The 1st or 2nd pullback of a fresh trend is the good trade. By the 4th–5th push — pullbacks shrinking, price far above its average — you're "buying a discount" at the top.
[YES] 1st–2nd pullback, trend has room → continue[NO] Old, stretched, exhausted trend → SKIP[NO] Daily chart disagrees with the trade ("counter-trend" flag) → SKIP

**Step 2. Was the leg real, organic buying?**
A good leg is a staircase of directional closes over several bars. A single giant news/gap spike is not a leg — there's no real buying underneath it to defend the pullback, and the "retrace" often just keeps going.
[YES] Organic staircase → continue[NO] One climactic spike → SKIP[NO] Can't instantly see where the leg starts/ends → SKIP (messy chart = fake fib)

**Step 3. Is the pullback slow and reluctant?**
This is the single most important Fib question: the pullback must move _differently_ from the leg. Same speed = reversal.
[YES] Slow drift → continue[NO] Fast slam → SKIP

**Step 4. Does the zone line up with something real?**
The percentages alone are weak. The zone is strong when it overlaps an old level that mattered — a former ceiling that should now act as a floor, an old gap, a daily-chart level ("D1 aligned" flag).
[YES] Zone + old structure → continue[WARN] Naked fib touch, nothing else there → needs everything else perfect

**Step 5. Is there a trap just below the zone?**
[YES] Nothing obvious below → continue[WARN] Trap below → widen stop past it (one edit) if reward survives, else SKIP

**Step 6. Is the reversal candle convincing?**
It should be at least average-sized, close near its high, and its wick should have actually poked into the zone. A tiny doji "reversal" is the market shrugging.
[YES] Decisive engulfing/hammer in the zone → continue[NO] Tiny or hesitant candle → SKIP

**Step 7. News & timing (from Start Here)**
[NO] Big release inside the trade's lifetime → SKIP[NO] Late Friday → SKIP[YES] Clear → continue
**All seven passed → TAKE.** The plan is pre-set: bank half at the old high, move stop to break-even, let the rest run. Don't replace that plan with a single nearby target — your own results punished it (see Lessons).

## EMA20 Fade — the Rubber-Band Trade (checklist)
## EMA20 Fade — the Rubber-Band Trade
Reward **1.3–2× risk**Wins **~55–62%**Fires most often — **easiest to over-trade**
**The idea in one sentence:** price closed unusually far from its 20-bar average (2+ ATRs — the rubber band is stretched) and printed a reversal candle back toward it; you fade the stretch, bank half at the average, run the rest. The whole picture:

**What the computer already checked (don't redo it)**
- The stretch is at least 2 ATRs from the average
- Trend-strength gauge (ADX) is below the danger line, and the extreme is **not** a fresh multi-week breakdown (hard-filtered — you won't see those)
- The trigger candle closed back toward the average; blended reward cleared 1.3× risk
**Read this first:** this alert fires the most and was the biggest bleeder in the blind-approve test. Your job here is **saying no**. In anything that looks like a trend, the default answer is NO.

### Walk these in order — any NO means SKIP

**Step 1. The freight-train test — would you step in front of this?**
The numbers already passed — but numbers lag. If your eyes say freight train, believe them over the gauge.
[YES] Calm, rangy chart → continue[NO] Freight train → SKIP

**Step 2. What created the stretch?**
An orderly drift away from the average reverts well. Two creators that don't: a **gap** (weekend/holiday hole in prices), and a **break** of an obvious level or of the lowest low you can see on the chart — breakout energy runs further.
[YES] Orderly excursion → continue[NO] Gap-made stretch → SKIP[NO] Fresh break of a visible level → SKIP[NO] News-spike stretch → SKIP

**Step 3. Momentum check: the last 3 bars into the extreme**
Three or more wide, full-bodied candles in a row pushing into the extreme = momentum, not exhaustion. Exhaustion looks like shrinking bodies and growing wicks.
[YES] Shrinking bars, wicks appearing → continue[NO] 3+ wide stacked candles → SKIP

**Step 4. Is the extreme at a real location?**
Best version: the stretch bottoms out exactly at yesterday's low / last week's low ("pool confluence" flag) — a reason for buyers to be there beyond the rubber band.
[YES] At a level → strong[WARN] Mid-air → the other steps must all be clean

**Step 5. Is the reward still there?**
The average is a _moving_ target — it drifts toward price. If the excursion was slow and the average has already come down to meet price, the snap-back is worth too little.
[YES] Average still meaningfully far → continue[NO] Average nearly reached price → SKIP

**Step 6. Have you already been told no?**
If this same stretch already stopped you out this week, the market is telling you it's a trend. Re-fading the same excursion needs dramatically better evidence, not hope.
[YES] First attempt → continue[NO] Second fade of the same move → SKIP
**All six passed → TAKE.** Plan is pre-set: bank half at the average, stop to break-even, runner to the far side. In a trending regime you should be skipping most of these — that's the strategy working, not you being timid.

## Edit rules + candle tells
## Editing a trade — one change, one reason
The dialog keeps reward-to-risk locked: edit one level, the other follows, size re-computes. Three legitimate edits exist. Anything more = the setup is bad, skip it.
| Edit | When | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| **Widen the stop** | The proposed stop sits just _inside_ an obvious level or round number where a stab is likely | Move it just **beyond** the structure and accept the smaller size. Your data agrees: structural widens have paid; tiny "comfort" widens (≤10 pips) are 0-for-6 — either clear the level or leave it alone. |
| **Pull the target closer** | A major level or round number sits just _before_ the proposed target | Take profit in front of the wall. But: your TP pulls are 0-for-2 so far (see Lessons) — only do this for a concrete visible obstacle, never for comfort, and never replace a bank-half-and-run plan with one near target. |
| **Improve the entry** (pending orders) | A better fill is likely and you accept possibly missing the trade | A better entry that never fills costs 0. Never chase after it misses. |
**Never:** risk above 1% · tighten the stop to buy more size · stretch the target on a feeling · more than one edit per trade.

## Judging any trigger candle — 3 questions
| Pattern | Means | Good version |
|---|---|---|
| **Engulfing** | One side overwhelmed the other in a single bar | Big body, closes near its extreme, swallows several bars — not one doji |
| **Hammer / pin** | A level was stabbed and rejected | The wick actually pierced the level, then snapped back; close in the far third |
| **Full-body drive** | Conviction — this is what a real "shift" looks like | Tiny wicks, often leaves a gap; its absence on an SMC shift = skip |
| **Doji** | Indecision where you needed conviction | There isn't one — a doji trigger is the market shrugging → lean skip |
For any candle: **where** did it print (at a level, or mid-air)? **how big** is it vs. the last 20 bars? **where did it close** in its own range?

## Correlated families — one bet, not several
| Family | Members | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| USD block | every USD pair; gold & indices move inversely | Long EURUSD + long GBPUSD + short USDCHF ≈ 3× one short-dollar bet |
| EUR crosses | EURUSD, EURGBP, EURJPY, EURAUD… | share the EUR leg |
| JPY crosses | USDJPY, EURJPY, GBPJPY, AUDJPY… | risk mood moves them together, violently |
| Risk-on block | AUD, NZD, indices; CHF/JPY inverse | index long + AUDJPY long = one bet |
| Metals | XAUUSD, XAGUSD | silver is gold with leverage |
**Caps:** FTMO hard limits — daily loss 5% ($1,250), total 10% ($2,500); five straight 1% losers in a day breaches. System: ≤3% open+armed at once. Yours: one family = one idea = max 2%.

## Reading the event lines
| Situation | Do |
|---|---|
| High-impact event ahead, within ~12h | **Skip or wait.** A swing entry hours before CPI is a coin flip. |
| Minor event ahead | Trade normally. |
| Recent event behind, bias arrow _agrees_ with you | Mild plus. |
| Recent event behind, bias arrow _against_ you | You're fading fresh fundamentals — demand an A-grade chart. |
| Setup created by the event candle itself | Lean skip — post-news moves extend and reverse violently. |
| Indices / gold / oil | USD events are your events. |

## Jargon → your chart
| Term you'll hear | On your chart |
|---|---|
| Liquidity / stop hunt | the labelled pool lines and the sweep through them |
| Buy-side / sell-side liquidity | pools above price / below price (targets) |
| MSS / CHoCH | the "MSS ✓" break of the last small swing |
| Displacement | the big-bodied leg that makes the shift believable |
| Fair value gap / imbalance | the shaded 3-bar gap boxes |
| Order block | the shaded entry-zone rectangle |
| Premium / discount / OTE | the fib grid; the shaded 61.8–78.6 band is the discount zone |
| Kill zones | bar time in UTC: London 07–13, NY 13–20 — sweeps there mean more than overnight ones |
